facts.content: 3-day history of watery diarrhea, occurring 6–7 times a day, requiring proximity to toilet and affecting work and activities of daily living.
facts.source_text: CC: 3-day hx watery diarrhea (~6–7/day); needs proximity to toilet; affecting work/ADLs

facts.content: Patient experiences watery, loose stools with no blood.
Patient has intermittent, crampy abdominal pain in the left lower quadrant which is non-radiating.
facts.source_text: LLQ crampy abdo pain, intermittent; non-radiating

facts.content: Patient reports a decreased appetite but is tolerating fluids and eating soups or smoothies.
Patient felt hot at the onset of symptoms but is currently afebrile.
facts.source_text: Felt hot at onset; afebrile currently

facts.content: Patient ate Chinese takeaway 4 days ago and one child vomited after but did not have diarrhea.
facts.source_text: Ate Chinese takeaway 4 days ago; one child vomited (no diarrhea)

facts.content: Patient has a well-controlled asthma condition.
Patient works as an accountant and lives with wife and two kids.
facts.source_text: SH: Accountant; lives w/ wife + 2 kids

facts.content: Patient is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol.

Suspected acute gastroenteritis, possibly viral or bacterial, and possibly foodborne, with 3 days of watery diarrhea occurring 6-7 times a day, left lower quadrant cramps, initial vomiting now resolved, no blood, and tolerating fluids.
facts.source_text: Suspected acute gastroenteritis (viral vs bacterial; possible foodborne). 3 days watery diarrhea 6–7/day, LLQ cramps, initial emesis now resolved, no blood, tolerating fluids.

facts.content: Advised conservative management with oral hydration and oral rehydration solutions like Dioralyte.
facts.source_text: Conservative mgmt: oral hydration; ORS (e.g., Dioralyte)

facts.content: Paracetamol 2 tablets up to four times a day as needed for fever or aches during the first few days.
facts.source_text: Paracetamol 2 tabs up to QID prn fever/aches (first few days)

facts.content: Advised rest and to take 2-3 days off work.
No antibiotics prescribed at this stage.
Follow-up advised if not improving in 3-4 days or worsening.
facts.source_text: F/U if not improving in 3–4 days or worsening

facts.content: If symptoms persist, consider stool studies and sending a stool sample.
facts.source_text: If persistent, consider stool studies (send stool sample)
